title: Call Stack and Function Execution

understand.concept: A call stack tracks active function calls in a last-in, first-out order. When one function calls another, the new call becomes active; it completes or returns before the earlier caller continues in ordinary synchronous execution. Each active call has its own execution context, including parameters and local variables.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding the call stack helps trace nested calls, locate errors, and explain recursion. Deep call chains consume resources and may exceed a runtime's stack limit.
understand.analogy: A stack of trays: the newest tray is handled first, and when it is removed the tray below becomes available. Actual execution contexts contain more information than a tray and are runtime-managed.
understand.analogyLimit: This analogy omits language-specific implementation details; use it only as a first mental model.

explain.narrative: Follow nested calls from the first caller down to the deepest active call. The last function called is the next one to complete; after it returns, control resumes in the previous function. Stack traces help identify which calls were active when an error occurred.

examples.explanation: The inner add call returns before twice receives its argument.

examples.title: Each call has local values
examples.code:
function show(n) { console.log(n); if(n>1) show(n-1); }
show(3);
examples.explanation: Recursive calls have separate active parameter values.

examples.title: Return to caller
examples.explanation: After inner returns, outer assigns the result and continues.

examples.title: Stack trace concept
examples.explanation: When an error occurs, a stack trace can show the chain of calls leading to it.
